q: The following Articles of the Indian Constitution deal with Parliament:
explanation:
Most books and keys: Articles 79-123. Strictly, Chapter II of Part V (Parliament) is Arts. 79-122; Art. 123 (ordinances) is in Chapter III (Laxmikanth).
NextGen says Articles 79 to 123 of Part V deal with Parliament, the key's answer; the other ranges cut across the Executive (Arts. 52-78) and the Judiciary.

notes.text: - **Lok Sabha – Art. 83(2)**: **5 years from its first meeting**; may be **dissolved earlier** by the President on the PM's advice. During a National Emergency it can be extended by law **one year at a time**, not beyond **6 months** after the Emergency ends (5th LS, 1971–77).

q: 'Indian Parliament' means
options: The President, the Prime Minister and the Rajya Sabha
Elected members of the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha
The President and the two Houses of Parliament
key_text: The President and the two Houses of Parliament
explanation: Art. 79: Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses – the President is part of it although not a member.

notes.text: - **Rajya Sabha – Art. 83(1)**: a **permanent House**, **never dissolved** (not even by the President); **one-third of members retire every second year**; a member's **6-year** term is fixed by the **RPA, 1951**; casual vacancy filled for the rest of the term; first RS (1952) – retirees chosen by **lottery**.

q: Identify the odd one.
explanation: The Lok Sabha is a constitutional House (Arts. 79, 81); the Planning Commission, NDC and Deputy Prime Minister have no constitutional basis, so the LS is the odd one.

notes.text: - **Normally three sessions a year** – **Budget, Monsoon, Winter** (Art. 85 only caps the gap at six months).

q: Though he/she is not a Member of Parliament of India, but he/she is an integral part of Indian Parliament - Who?
explanation: Under Art. 79 Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses; the President is not a member of either House but is an integral part of Parliament.

notes.text: - **Rajya Sabha – Art. 83(1)**: a **permanent House**, **never dissolved** (not even by the President); **one-third of members retire every second year**; a member's **6-year** term is fixed by the **RPA, 1951**; casual vacancy filled for the rest of the term; first RS (1952) – retirees chosen by **lottery**.

q: Who constitutes the Parliament of India?
explanation: Art. 79: Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses – so the President is a constituent part of Parliament. The Supreme Court and elections do not 'constitute' it.

notes.text: - **Rajya Sabha – Art. 83(1)**: a **permanent House**, **never dissolved** (not even by the President); **one-third of members retire every second year**; a member's **6-year** term is fixed by the **RPA, 1951**; casual vacancy filled for the rest of the term; first RS (1952) – retirees chosen by **lottery**.

q: Who designed the Parliament House at New Delhi?
explanation: Parliament House (Sansad Bhavan) was designed by Herbert Baker (with Edwin Lutyens), built 1921-27.

q: Rajya Sabha can take initiative in
options: None of the given answers is correct
key_text: None of the given answers is correct
explanation: None: censure of ministers lies with the Lok Sabha, Money Bills start only in the LS and judges are appointed by the President. The RS's own initiatives are Arts. 249, 312 and VP removal.

q: A bill becomes a law when
options: The Council of Ministers approves it
The two Houses of Parliament approve it by majority of votes
The Supreme Court upholds its constitutional validity
explanation: A Bill passed by both Houses becomes an Act only when the President gives assent (Art. 111); passage by the Houses alone is not enough.

notes.text: - Kuldip Singh = Delimitation Commission; **Kuldip Nayar** = RS domicile case (2006).

q: Rajya Sabha has special powers when compared to Lok Sabha. In relation to this, choose the wrong answer?
options: Rajya Sabha is a permanent body
Resolution related to the removal of Vice president shall be first introduced in Rajya Sabha
For Constitutional amendment both houses have same power
Rajya Sabha has the exclusive authority in approving National Emergency
key_text: Rajya Sabha has the exclusive authority in approving National Emergency
explanation: Wrong: approving a National Emergency is done by both Houses (the RS has no exclusive authority; it alone acts only when the LS is dissolved). The RS is permanent, VP removal begins in the RS, and both Houses have equal power on amendments.

q: Impeachment proceedings against the Vice President can be initiated
explanation: Art. 67(b): a resolution to remove the Vice-President can be moved only in the Rajya Sabha and must be agreed to by the Lok Sabha.

q:
The equal status of the Rajya Sabha with the Lok Sabha can be described by which of the following statement/statements?
I. Introduction and passage of Money Bills.
II. Consideration of the CAG's report
III. Initiating the removal of the Vice-President.
IV. Approval of proclamation of all the three types of emergencies by the President.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
explanation: The Houses are equal in considering CAG reports and approving all three emergencies (II and IV); Money Bills are LS-only and removal of the VP starts only in the RS.

q: Who has the power to create new All India Services in India?
explanation: Art. 312: new All-India Services are created by Parliament only after a Rajya Sabha resolution by two-thirds present and voting – a special power of the RS.
